craft_claim: Nostalgic voice speaks from two temporal positions at once - the remembering now and the remembered then. The craft signature is controlled shuttling between them (tense shifts, psychic distance, a sensory bridge) that keeps both frames audible; collapsing into either plain reminiscence or raw scene without the present self kills the tone.

supporting_evidence.location: European Journal of Social Psychology 45(1):52-61, Studies 3-4
supporting_evidence.note: The emotion's defining achievement is linking a present self to a past self; a narrative rendering must keep both temporal positions in view for that link to be felt by the reader.

None of nostalgia's 18 central or 17 peripheral features refers to the present or future - the concept is entirely memory-anchored, while the feeling itself is appraised now. Two positions by definition: the then that supplies the content and the now that feels the pull.

The memory-anchored, past-referential core holds across cultures, so the two-position structure is a property of the emotion rather than an English idiom - it should be stageable in any language's prose.

supporting_evidence.location: Opening pages of Swann's Way: the madeleine-and-tea episode (described, not quoted)
supporting_evidence.note: A present sensation unexpectedly opens the past; the scene is narrated by a present-tense-positioned narrator who is seized by recollection, so listener and memory occupy the page simultaneously. The sensory bridge is the mechanism that welds the two frames.

An exiled speaker addresses a cloud that will reach his wife: present separation, remembered intimacy, and a hoped-for future arrival are all held in one address. The two-position requirement is met by dramatic situation rather than by retrospective narration - proof the mechanism is not English-tense-bound.

scope: Craft inference from psychology and exemplars; no study isolates nostalgic prose syntax. Cross-link (read-only): clm-point-of-view-psychic-distance. Feeds card section 5.
exceptions: Verse and lyric forms can sustain the two positions structurally (address, apostrophe) where prose needs tense and focalization.
